title: microflow-surface-topology-and-entry-contracts-notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects exploratory thinking and lightweight wireframes for a microflow-driven console surface topology. Goal is to define clear entry contracts for user journeys (task entry -> short task flow -> deep page) so the sidebar and routing can be simplified while preserving discoverability and keyboard-first access.

Background/context:
- Current problem: too many first-level routes in the left rail; users report cognitive overhead when switching between workflows (models, deployments, logs, rollouts).
- Console team hypothesis: consolidating entry points into compact microflows (task-first entry tiles + transient surface) will reduce route cardinality without harming direct access to power features.
- Constraints: must work with existing rollout tooling, Dedicated/Private product variations, and accessibility (screen reader focus order + reduced motion).

High-level goals:
1) Reduce permanent top-level items from ~12 -> ~6 while enabling rapid access to the rest via contextual microflows and command palette.
2) Ensure keyboard-first paths to any page within 2 keystrokes from anywhere (Cmd-K -> entry or / -> quick task).
3) Maintain traceability for audits: route transitions must preserve request context (customer id, model version) so back/forward works predictably.
4) Support graceful degradation: when capacity-sensitive features are unavailable, surface a read-only or fallback variant without breaking nav contract.

Microflow concepts (terminology):
- Entry tile: compact tile in the left rail that opens a surface overlay (microflow surface) with 3–6 primary actions.
- Microflow surface: ephemeral panel anchored to rail; contains short task flow (e.g., create deployment, view traces, run eval).
- Surface contract: lightweight JSON-ish contract (route params, initial focus, context hints) that defines how a microflow opens and how it hands off to a full page.
- Handoff: the transition from microflow surface to canonical page; must preserve keyboard focus and route state.

Wireframe writeup (textual sketches):
1) Compact rail (collapsed by default for new accounts): 6 tiles vertically (Home, Workflows, Models, Deploy, Monitor, Settings). Hover/expand shows labels.
2) Clicking Models -> opens microflow surface with tabs: 'Catalog', 'Pins', 'Import', 'Quantize'. Each item has 1-line descriptions and keyboard accelerators (1,2,3,4).
3) Deploy tile -> surface provides 'New deployment', 'Dedicated settings', 'Autoscale preview'. New deployment is a 3-step inline flow (model select -> capacity profile -> quick checks).
4) Monitor tile -> surface shows recent alerts, quick traces, and a 'Go to full traces' link (handoff).

Routing and surface contract examples (pseudo):
- entry=deploy; contract={"context":{"model_id":"m-123"},"focus":"capacity-profile","backTarget":"/projects/p-99/models"}
- Microflow surface should map to a shallow URL fragment so opening the surface is navigable (e.g., /?microflow=deploy&context=m-123) and deep links to the full page should use canonical URL /projects/p-99/deployments/new?model=m-123

Accessibility + keyboard rules:
- Microflow surfaces are modal-lite: do not trap focus, but set initial focus to first actionable element. Escape closes surface to previous focus.
- Screen reader announcements: "Opened Deploy surface: create new deployment, step 1 of 3".
- Reduced motion: avoid large motion for rail expansion; prefer crossfade + instant transform for keyboard users.
- All actions must be reachable via keyboard shortcuts: Cmd-K -> type 'deploy' -> Enter opens deploy surface; within surface use numbers or Tab to reach actions.

Edge cases and failover behavior:
- If service unavailable (e.g., dedicated capacity API 503), surface shows 'Restricted' state with fallback actions: view docs, request quota, open readonly view.
- If user navigates deep into a canonical page then presses back, they should return to the microflow surface state rather than raw rail. Back navigation must preserve the previous contract.
- Mobile: convert left rail to bottom sheet with the same microflow tiles; surfaces become full-screen sheets.

Backlog/grooming (proposed JIRA tasks and priority):
- PROD-4268 (P0): Implement microflow surface anchor component + shallow URL handling. Owner: Rui. Est: 5 dev days.
- PROD-4281 (P0): Keyboard accelerator mapping + Cmd-K integration. Owner: Liam. Est: 3 dev days.
- PROD-4302 (P1): Accessibility announcements + reduced motion opt-in. Owner: Samira. Est: 4 dev days.
- PROD-4310 (P1): Devops: fallback states for capacity endpoints. Owner: Ethan. Est: 2 dev days.
- PROD-4335 (P2): Analytics: event taxonomy for microflow open/handoff. Owner: Aisha. Est: 2 dev days.

Acceptance criteria (for initial experiment):
- Left rail shows 6 tiles; telemetry shows decrease in 'nav friction' metric (measured via time-to-first-action) by >= 10% in A/B test.
- Cmd-K + typed command opens correct microflow with focus landed.
- Handoff to canonical page preserves context (model id, project id) and back returns to surface state.
- No accessibility violations flagged by axe-core automated check for common flows.

Open questions / discussion points (for next grooming):
- Which items should remain permanent vs microflow-only? (ex: 'Billing' is likely permanent for enterprises).
- Do we allow nested microflows (microflow opening another microflow) or restrict depth to 1?
- How to represent RBAC differences between Hosted/Dedicated/Private in the microflow surface without overwhelming the small surface?
- Measurement plan: what events exactly to fire for handoff vs microflow open vs canonical page load? (Ping: analytics team)

Design quick wins / experiments to run first 2 sprints:
1) Build a static prototype (Figma + keyboard prototyping) of Deploy/Models microflows and run 10 remote usability sessions.
2) Implement shallow URL + microflow component behind feature flag and ship to 10% of org accounts.
3) Add analytics for microflow-open, action-select, handoff, fallback-state.

Next steps (owners):
- Aisha: schedule 1-week prototype sprint with Product Design, include 10 usability sessions (by 2024-10-11).
- Rui: spike for shallow URL and surface prototype (deliverable: working component + doc for route contract by 2024-10-04).
- Liam: draft keyboard shortcut map and add to global cmd-k index (by 2024-10-08).
- Samira: write accessibility test checklist and run on prototype (by 2024-10-11).

Notes to self / crumbs:
- Keep microflow copy short; avoid nested menus inside the surface.
- Consider 'pin to rail' affordance for power users (drag surface action -> pin -> creates a permanent rail item).
- Reuse existing rollout/fallback patterns from Monitor/Alerts to keep consistent UX.

References:
- Related PRD: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PRD/Console+Navigation+Goals
- Past experiments: PROD-3782 (compact-rail A/B test) — results summary linked in Confluence page above.

End of notes.
__notes: working doc - iterate freely; will extract a follow-up PRD if prototype signals positive metrics
